objectives: Define governance, risk and compliance by the question each one answers
Recognize the costs of a fragmented program
Describe the roles in the IIA Three Lines Model
Check a program against five signs of maturity

checks.q: A company runs separate teams for SOC 2, ISO 27001 and HIPAA, each with its own control list and evidence folder. What is the main problem this creates?
options: The frameworks conflict, so the company cannot hold a SOC 2 report and an ISO 27001 certificate in the same year.
Shared controls are evidenced once per framework, evidence goes stale between audits, and no one sees the whole program.
HIPAA forbids sharing controls with other frameworks, so the three teams must stay separate and keep their own evidence.
Auditors reject any evidence collected by a different team, so each team must re-collect its own before every audit.
checks.why: Nothing stops an organization holding both a SOC 2 report and an ISO 27001 certificate. The cost of silos is duplication, stale point-in-time evidence and reporting that cannot show the whole program.

checks.q: Which question does the risk part of GRC answer?
options: Who owns each decision, and what have we formally committed to?
What are we required to do, and can we show that we do it?
What could go wrong, and is the remaining exposure acceptable?
Which framework should we pursue first, and who will audit it?
checks.why: Governance answers who decides and what was committed to; compliance answers what is required and whether it can be shown; risk answers what could go wrong and whether the exposure is within appetite.

checks.q: In the IIA Three Lines Model, who provides independent and objective assurance to the governing body?
options: The first line: the managers who run the controls day to day
The second line: the security, risk and compliance functions
The third line: internal audit, independent of management
The external auditor, acting as part of the second line
checks.why: Internal audit is the third line, and its value comes from independence from management. External auditors sit outside the model, though they rely on it.

checks.q: A risk was "accepted" in a leadership meeting last year. Which detail matters most for the decision to stand up later?
options: That the meeting had a quorum and the vote was unanimous
A record of who decided, why, and when it will be reviewed
That the risk was first scored on a standard five-by-five matrix
That every attendee signed the printed minutes afterward
checks.why: An accepted risk is only defensible if it is attributable, explained and time-bound. Without those three, the acceptance cannot be reviewed, renewed or challenged.
